messages.subject: Release of seewave 2.0.5
messages.body_plain:
Dear seewave users,

A new minor version of seewave (2.0.5) has been pushed to CRAN right
now. The version of each OS should be available soon.

Please see the changes listed below.

Enjoy,

Jerome

---

OTHER CHANGES
o autoc(): a bug fixed when using 'threshold'.
o drawfilter(): a bug of the axis labels fixed.
o fma(): slighty improved by trying to remove DC component.
o fund(): the default value of 'fmax' is now f/2.
o NDSI(): the argument 'anthrophony' is renamed 'anthropophony'.
o spectro(): a bug introduced in the last version regarding the display
of the time axis fixed.

messages.subject: general question about entropy
messages.body_plain:
Hi everybody,

My understanding of entropy is that it's the uncertainty in a scenario, so if there are equal chances of an outcome occurring, entropy is at its maximum because there's no way we could predict an outcome. Following this logic, why is it that noisy signals trend higher in the acoustic entropy index compared to simpler waveforms? If I plot the PMF of the amplitude for a simple sine wave, it looks like there is a relatively equal probability of any one amplitude occurring. Can someone explain to me what I'm missing?

Thanks

Sean

Dear all,

I want to display multiple sonograms in the same figure. I have tried the following:

som1<-readWave("CS1.wav")
som2<-readWave("CS2.wav")
som3<-readWave("CS3.wav")
som4<-readWave("CS4.wav")
som5<-readWave("guentheri.wav")
som6<-readWave("henselii.wav")

png("todos_cantos.png",width=6000,height=9000,res=600)

par(mfrow=c(3,2))

spectro(som1,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2)

spectro(som2,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2)

spectro(som3,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2)

spectro(som4,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2)

spectro(som5,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2)

spectro(som6,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2)

messages.subject: Re: Display multiple sonograms in the same figure
messages.subject_clean: Display multiple sonograms in the same figure
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I encounter the exact same problem days ago. I was using mfrow and it did not work.

It turned out that the function spectro() return two plots: the sonogram and the amplitude level
As Jesse mentioned, the way to do it is to use layout() with the argument scale=F

if you want the dB scale for each graph then I would suggest something like this

dev.off() # just to make sure that there is no previous layout
layout(matrix(c(1:12), nrow = 3, byrow = T), width = rep(c(3, 1), 3)) #set the layout, notice that the number of columns double because one column is for the spectrogram and another column for the dB scale (the small one)
par(mar = c()) # adjust the margin to your need if need be otherwise ignore this line

spectro(som1,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2, scale = F) # plot only the sonogram
dBscale(collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2) # plot the dB scale of that particular sonogram
spectro(som2,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2, scale = F)
dBscale(collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2)
spectro(som3,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2, scale = F)
dBscale(collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2)
spectro(som4,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2, scale = F)
dBscale(collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2)
spectro(som5,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2, scale = F)
dBscale(collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2)
spectro(som6,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2, scale = F)
dBscale(collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2)

The dB scale may look redundant in that case. Instead, I would recommend something like this:

dev.off() # just to make sure that there is no previous layout
layout(matrix(c(1:3, 4, 5:7, 4, 8:10, 4), nrow = 3, byrow = T), width = c(3, 3, 3, 1)) #set the layout, the far right column will extent from top to bottom and will be reserved for the dB scale
par(mar = c()) # adjust the margin to your need if need be otherwise ignore this line

spectro(som1,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2, scale = F) # plot only the sonogram
spectro(som2,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2, scale = F)
spectro(som3,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2, scale = F)
dBscale(collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2) # plot the db scale at the far left all the way top to bottom
spectro(som4,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2, scale = F)
spectro(som5,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2, scale = F)
spectro(som6,osc=TRUE, f=44100, wl=512, ovlp=75, flim=c(0,6), collevels=seq(-35,0,0.1), palette=reverse.gray.colors.2, scale = F)

messages.subject: amplitude and signal noise ration using the function env()
messages.subject_clean: amplitude and signal noise ration using the function env()
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

First of all, I am newby to bioacoustic so please excuse my ignorance.

According to R's help, env() returns the amplitude envelope

While using env() with the argument scale = F and envt = "abs" (I am interested in the absolute value), my questions are:
Does the amplitude envelope from the function env() has a unit (is it mV or dB or I do not know). I looked at the result and, to me, it does not seem to be in dB because the values are too big
Assuming that it is not in dB, how to convert them in dB? can I use the code below

amp.env <- env(wave)
amp.env.dB <- 10 * log10(amp.env)
I am having a doubt with that code because there is no reference and usually something is in dB because it was scaled to certain value.

Thanks,

Haja

Thanks
